name: CIS Critical Security Controls
description: The CIS Critical Security Controls v8 is a prioritized set of 18 Controls (153 Safeguards) for defending against pervasive cyber attacks. v8 reorganized from v7.1's 20 Controls into 18, consolidated some, and added cloud and mobile-specific safeguards. Safeguards are organized into three Implementation Groups (IG1 ⊂ IG2 ⊂ IG3) representing increasing levels of cybersecurity maturity required to implement them. Each Safeguard specifies its asset type (devices, software, data, network, users), security function (identify, protect, detect, respond, recover), and applicability per Implementation Group.
relationToCloudSecurity: CIS Controls v8 added explicit cloud security safeguards in IG2/IG3 (e.g., Control 4 — Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software — includes safeguards for cloud-native configurations). Maps to CSA CCM, NIST CSF, and ISO 27001 via the published CIS Mappings.
relationToAISecurity: CIS Controls v8 does not specifically address AI workloads. AI systems that store, process, or transmit organizational data remain subject to CIS Controls regardless of implementation technology. CIS has not yet published AI-specific control extensions.

The same terms say a non-member may not "post any Non-Member CIS Product on any website" or "create any derivative work based directly on an Non-Member CIS Product". The source XLSX files come from CIS WorkBench after registration. Since 2026-11-13 this public repository holds only this metadata stub. Correction 2026-11-13: earlier metadata recorded CC-BY-4.0 and the README said CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; both were wrong (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 is the licence CIS states for the PDF CIS Benchmarks).

lifecycle.notes: v8 was current 2021-2024. v8.1 (June 2024) is now the active version with minor updates. v8 remains widely referenced in compliance documentation. The changelog extraction (cis-controls-v8-changelog.json, held in the private dataset) maps v8 → v7.1 for organizations migrating from older versions.

current_extraction.notes: This describes the extraction held in the private dataset (dataset-private-laws-regulations-standards, same path); none of its files are in this public repository. Extracted from the CIS-published XLSX (CIS_Controls_Version_8.xlsx) via scripts/parse_cis.py. The XLSX is the authoritative source; the JSON/CSV/MD are reproducible derivatives. The source XLSX is not committed anywhere (CIS WorkBench requires registration).

extraction_history.reason: Initial extraction from CIS WorkBench XLSX, promoted from dataset-private-laws-regulations-standards in 2026-05

notes: Originally extracted in dataset-private-laws-regulations-standards, moved to this public repository in 2026-05 on the mistaken reading that the CIS Controls are CC BY 4.0. Hosting: metadata-only in this public repository. The full text, page images, structured data and extraction scripts were removed on 2026-11-13 and are held in the private companion dataset (dataset-private-laws-regulations-standards, same path) under the 4-tier hosting rule (Kurt Seifried, 2026-11-09: free-login sources need his approval before public mirroring; paid or members-only sources are never mirrored publicly without an explicit, documented exception); this source is Tier 3 (CIS WorkBench registration required to download the source XLSX). On 2026-11-13 Kurt chose the option "Move all four (Recommended)". The content had been public here from this repository's first commit (2026-05-12) until then; it remains in git history, and whether to purge that history is a separate decision still pending. Records: CloudSecurityAlliance-DataSets/dataset-public-laws-regulations-standards#148, CloudSecurityAlliance-DataSets/dataset-private-laws-regulations-standards#15. Any return to public hosting needs an explicit, documented exception from Kurt, recorded as a public_exception object in this file (see METADATA-SCHEMA.md).

desired_end_state.notes: Full text held in dataset-private-laws-regulations-standards since 2026-11-13 (Tier 3 (CIS WorkBench registration required to download the source XLSX)). Public hosting needs an explicit, documented exception recorded as public_exception.
